annotation_description: Casting Consult the Star Charts before playing a land drop this turn is a sequencing error. With only 2 lands in play, Consult looks at 2 cards. If they played a land first (e.g., Mistrise Village, Restless Anchorage, or Sunbillow Verge), they'd have 3 lands and look at 3 cards instead, giving a strictly better selection. Additionally, casting it main phase rather than at end of opponent's turn means tapping out and being unable to hold up No More Lies or Get Lost.

Playing Mistrise Village tapped instead of Sunbillow Verge untapped leaves only 2 mana available this turn instead of 3, missing the ability to hold up Get Lost (1W) or No More Lies (WU) against the opponent's developing board (Formidable Speaker is already in play). Sunbillow Verge enters untapped since KimiK2 controls Plains (Meticulous Archive and Hallowed Fountain).

Cori Mountain Monastery produces only R and colorless, which doesn't help cast any spell in hand (Day of Judgment needs WW, No More Lies needs WU, Consult the Star Charts needs U). Sunbillow Verge enters untapped (controls Plains) and produces W, contributing toward Day of Judgment and maintaining better mana flexibility for the rest of the game.

The opponent has Overlord of the Balemurk with 5 time counters (impending), so it's not a creature yet and Day of Judgment won't hit it. The opponent has no creatures on board that need answering right now. Casting Consult the Star Charts is reasonable for card selection with 4 lands, seeing 4 cards. However, the player should consider whether playing a land first (Sunbillow Verge or Restless Anchorage) would be better to increase the number of cards seen by Consult the Star Charts (5 instead of 4). Playing a land first before casting the spell would give strictly more card selection.

Picked Hallowed Fountain over Aang's Iceberg from Consult the Star Charts. Aang's Iceberg is a premium flash removal spell that can exile Overlord of the Balemurk or any future threat, while KimiK2 already has two lands in hand (Sunbillow Verge and Restless Anchorage) for future land drops. The Iceberg would provide critical flexible interaction against the opponent's graveyard-heavy strategy.

GPT4om Stoic chose to copy Bringer of the Last Gift with Superior Spider-Man. While Bringer is a 6/6 flyer, copying it with Spider-Man makes it a 4/4 (Spider-Man's copy effect overrides P/T to 4/4). More importantly, Bringer's ETB says 'if you cast it' — since Spider-Man is being cast (not Bringer), the mass sacrifice + graveyard recursion trigger won't fire. So you get a 4/4 flyer but lose the Bringer from your graveyard permanently (it gets exiled). Formidable Speaker as a copy would give a 4/4 body with its ETB (discard to tutor a creature), which could find a key piece, and Formidable Speaker is far less valuable in the graveyard than Bringer. Exiling Bringer removes a key reanimation target for Overlord of the Balemurk's graveyard recursion and for actually casting Bringer later.

message: Pick triggered ability (goes to the stack first)
annotation_description: By choosing to put the Bringer of the Last Gift's ETB ability on the stack in a way that it resolved before Overlord of the Balemurk's trigger, GPT4om missed the opportunity to mill 4 cards first (via Overlord's ability) to stock the graveyard with additional creatures before Bringer's mass sacrifice and reanimate effect. Resolving Overlord's mill first could have put additional creature cards in the graveyard, which would then all come back when Bringer's ability resolved.

message: Discard a card and search your library for a creature card, reveal it, put it into your hand, then shuffle?
annotation_description: Discarding Bitter Triumph to Formidable Speaker's ETB ability wastes a premium removal spell. Bitter Triumph is one of the best removal spells in the format, destroying any creature or planeswalker at instant speed for just 2 mana. Meanwhile, cards like Ardyn (8 mana, very hard to cast) or Bringer of the Last Gift (8 mana) are far less likely to be castable in a reasonable timeframe and would be much better discard fodder.

Chose Harvester of Misery for Superior Spider-Man's copy ability when the opponent has no creatures on board, wasting the -2/-2 ETB trigger (which also could hurt own creatures). Deceit would have been a stronger choice, providing hand disruption (forcing opponent to discard a nonland card) against an opponent with a likely full hand and no board presence, or bounce effect for future utility.

The opponent has Overlord of the Balemurk (5/5 impending, likely still an enchantment with time counters but context suggests it may be a creature) and Superior Spider-Man (4/4) on the battlefield. KimiK2 Spike has Day of Judgment available with exactly 4 mana (2WW) using Meticulous Archive, Hallowed Fountain, and two other lands. However, playing Hallowed Fountain tapped (to save 2 life) uses the land drop without advancing the board. More critically, the player should consider casting Tishana's Tidebinder (2U, 3 mana) this turn to flash-counter a triggered ability, or cast Day of Judgment to clear the board of Superior Spider-Man immediately. By playing Hallowed Fountain instead of Restless Anchorage (which also enters tapped but provides a creature land for later), and not casting Day of Judgment this turn when they have the mana to do so (Meticulous Archive + Hallowed Fountain already on board give WW, plus Mistrise Village for colorless = 2WW with 4 lands), they're giving the opponent another attack step with their creatures. The player has 4 lands already untapped and could cast Day of Judgment right now before playing the land, clearing the opponent's threats. Playing a land first is fine sequencing, but the real issue is whether they follow up with Day of Judgment. Still, if they play Hallowed Fountain tapped, they now have 4 untapped lands but need 2WW - they'd have W (Hallowed Fountain already on board), W/U (Meticulous Archive), U (Mistrise Village), R (Cori Mountain) = only 1W available from existing untapped lands plus U and R. Actually, with the existing untapped lands: Meticulous Archive (W/U), Hallowed Fountain (W/U), Mistrise Village (U), Cori Mountain Monastery (R) = they can make WWU + R, which is enough for Day of Judgment (2WW). Playing another Hallowed Fountain tapped doesn't help cast DoJ this turn. They should cast Day of Judgment now with their 4 untapped lands to clear Superior Spider-Man before it attacks.

The opponent has two creatures on board (Overlord of the Balemurk and Superior Spider-Man). KimiK2 Spike has Day of Judgment in hand which would destroy both enemy creatures cleanly. Instead, they cast Tishana's Tidebinder as a vanilla 3/2 (there's no activated/triggered ability to counter right now), which doesn't meaningfully impact the board against a 5/5 and a 4/4. Worse, casting Tidebinder before Day of Judgment means either they waste their own creature to the wrath next turn, or they delay the wrath and take significant combat damage from the opponent's large creatures. Day of Judgment would have been the correct play here - it cleanly answers both threats for 4 mana (which they have available via their 5 lands). Playing the Tidebinder first is poor sequencing that either wastes a card or delays a necessary board wipe.

GPT4om targeted their own Superior Spider-Man (4/4) with Harvester of Misery's -2/-2 discard ability instead of the opponent's Tishana's Tidebinder (3/2), which would have died to the -2/-2. Tidebinder was likely suppressing Overlord of the Balemurk's abilities, so killing it would both remove an opponent's creature and restore those abilities.

GPT4om Stoic sacrificed Superior Spider-Man, which was likely a copy of Harvester of Misery (effectively a 4/4 with menace and useful abilities), instead of the much less impactful Formidable Speaker (2/4 with no cards to discard for its ETB). The Spider-Man was the stronger board presence and combat threat.

Casting a second Formidable Speaker (2/4) when Deceit (5/5) was castable with available mana. Deceit with {B}{B} could strip a key card from the opponent's hand (likely holding countermagic or removal given 6 untapped lands and no board presence), while also presenting a much larger threat. The opponent having empty board but full hand suggests they're holding answers.

message: Discard a card and search your library for a creature card, reveal it, put it into your hand, then shuffle?
annotation_description: Discarding Bringer of the Last Gift to Formidable Speaker's tutor ability is a significant mistake. Bringer of the Last Gift is one of GPT4om's most powerful cards - a 6/6 flyer that when cast, forces all players to sacrifice their creatures and then returns all creature cards from graveyards to the battlefield. With the graveyard already stocked with Harvester of Misery x2, Superior Spider-Man, and Formidable Speaker, Bringer would be a devastating play that wipes the opponent's board while returning a massive army. The graveyard already has good creatures to recur, and Overlord of the Balemurk can mill more. Meanwhile, the duplicate Ardyn copies are less useful (legendary rule means only one can be on the battlefield), making one of them the natural discard choice.

With Overlord of the Balemurk (MV 5 Elemental) on the battlefield, Sunderflock's cost would be reduced by 5, making it castable for 4UU (6 mana). Sunderflock would provide a 5/5 flyer that bounces all non-Elemental creatures when cast - a powerful board control option. Already having one Deceit in hand makes a second copy less valuable, especially when Sunderflock offers a uniquely powerful effect at an efficient cost given the board state.

The opponent has Overlord of the Balemurk (with time counters ticking down), two Formidable Speakers on board, and a graveyard full of powerful creatures including Bringer of the Last Gift, Superior Spider-Man, Harvester of Misery, and Deceit. KimiK2 is at 18 life facing an increasingly threatening board. Day of Judgment would clear the two Formidable Speakers and is available right now for 4 mana (which KimiK2 has with 6 lands). More critically, casting Consult the Star Charts now for 2 mana (unkicked, so only looking at top 6 and taking 1 card) is mediocre value and doesn't address the board. The opponent's creatures are tapped so there's no immediate pressure, but the Overlord will become a 5/5 creature soon and the graveyard is stacking up with threats. However, the bigger issue is sequencing: KimiK2 should play a land first (Restless Anchorage or Steam Vents) before casting spells to maximize the number of cards seen with Consult the Star Charts. Playing a 7th land means seeing 7 cards instead of 6. Additionally, the reasoning mentions 'drawing two cards' but Consult the Star Charts unkicked only puts one card into hand, suggesting a misunderstanding of the card.

Chose Steam Vents as the second card when they already have one in hand. Restless Anchorage would serve as both a mana source and a win condition (creature land), which is very valuable for a control deck that needs to close games. The player already has adequate color fixing.

Casting Deceit precombat main phase requires tapping both Formidable Speakers to untap lands for mana, meaning no attacks this turn. The opponent has 3 untapped lands including W/U sources, meaning they could have No More Lies or other countermagic. Tapping out into open counter mana while giving up combat pressure is risky.

GPT4om Stoic named 'Frog' for Cavern of Souls, which is a completely irrelevant creature type. They have two copies of Ardyn, the Usurper in hand (which is a Human Noble) and Deceit (which is an Elemental Incarnation). Their deck appears to contain Demons, Humans, and other creature types but not Frogs. Naming 'Human' would help cast Ardyn (which costs 5BBB and is legendary, so only one copy matters, but making it uncounterable against the UW opponent with counterspells like No More Lies is significant). Alternatively, naming 'Demon' for future Demon creatures could be relevant. The opponent is playing a UW deck with counterspells, so the uncounterable clause on Cavern of Souls is very valuable, and it's completely wasted by naming Frog.

Played Restless Anchorage (enters tapped) instead of Sunbillow Verge (which would enter untapped since they control Plains via Hallowed Fountain). This costs 1 mana this turn. With Day of Judgment to cast at {2}{W}{W}, playing Sunbillow Verge untapped would leave 3 mana open after DoJ instead of 2, giving more flexibility for countermagic backup.

Casting Harvester of Misery when the opponent has no creatures means the -2/-2 ETB only hits GPT4om's own two Formidable Speakers (making them 0/2 until end of turn), preventing them from dealing any combat damage this turn. The opponent's board is empty so the -2/-2 provides zero value.

GPT4om Stoic has Overlord of the Balemurk (5/5) and two Formidable Speakers on the battlefield, with the opponent at 13 life and an empty board (no creatures). The opponent has 7 lands but no creatures to block. Attacking with all available creatures would deal significantly more damage. Overlord of the Balemurk is a 5/5 creature that could attack for 5 damage alongside the Formidable Speaker's 2 damage, dealing 7 total instead of just 2. The opponent has open mana but no creatures on board, so there's no unfavorable block scenario. One Formidable Speaker is tapped so can't attack, but Overlord of the Balemurk is untapped and should have attacked.

GPT4om Stoic used Formidable Speaker's untap ability targeting Harvester of Misery instead of a land that could provide additional mana. With Ardyn (8 mana, BBB), Deceit (6 mana), Formidable Speaker (3 mana), and Overlord (5 mana) in hand, untapping a black-producing land could have enabled casting additional spells this turn, such as Formidable Speaker or contributing toward Deceit/Overlord.

message: Discard a card and search your library for a creature card, reveal it, put it into your hand, then shuffle?
annotation_description: Discarded Deceit instead of the redundant second copy of Ardyn, the Usurper. Deceit has an evoke cost of just {U/B}{U/B} (2 mana), providing cheap interaction (bounce a permanent or force a discard) which is valuable when most lands are tapped. The second Ardyn is legendary and redundant - only one can be on the battlefield at a time.

Get Lost is targeting Harvester of Misery, but Harvester of Misery is in the opponent's graveyard, not on the battlefield. Looking at the opponent's battlefield, the threats are Overlord of the Balemurk (tapped), two Formidable Speakers (tapped), and lands. At 3 life, the critical threat is Overlord of the Balemurk which will become a 5/5 creature soon (it had 5 impending counters, 2 were removed in prior turns, so it likely has 0-1 counters left and is already a creature given it's listed without impending notation). Day of Judgment would clear all three creatures at once and is available. Using Get Lost on a single creature while Day of Judgment is available and would handle all threats is a significant waste of resources, especially at 3 life where the opponent giving you two Map tokens is irrelevant compared to clearing the whole board.

GPT4om Stoic has lethal on board with two Formidable Speakers (2+2=4 damage) against an opponent at 3 life with no blockers. Casting Overlord of the Balemurk precombat is unnecessary and gives the opponent additional information and interaction windows before the lethal attack.

GPT4om Stoic used Formidable Speaker's untap ability ({1}, {T}: Untap another target permanent) but targeted Meticulous Archive, an opponent's land. This gives the opponent a free untap on one of their lands, providing them with additional mana or options. The ability should be used to untap one of their own permanents for value, or not used at all. With Harvester of Misery on the stack (which gives other creatures -2/-2 on ETB), untapping their own Formidable Speaker or a land would have been far more useful. Untapping an opponent's land is actively harmful.

Opponent is at 3 life with no creatures on board. Attacking with both Overlord of the Balemurk (5/5) and Formidable Speaker (2/4) would deal 7 damage total, which is lethal through any single blocker the opponent could produce (e.g., activating Restless Anchorage as a 2/3). Attacking with only Overlord risks the opponent blocking with an activated Restless Anchorage to survive at 3 life.
